human CMV contains ser/thr protein phosphatase (PP) activities, including PP1 and PP2a.
purified CMV particles contain protein phosphatases that are responsible for hypophosphorylating cellular proteins within 30 min after contact between CMVs and the cell membrane.
CMV contains protein phosphatase 1 and protein phosphatase2A, which are active in purified virions and in infected cells.

the identification of the protein phosphatases associated with human cytomegaloviruses, and with their role in the early events after contact between the viral particle and the host cell membrane.
the identification of the protein phosphatase(s) found in purified CMV and with the characterization of their role in the hyper-immediate-earl events.
the study of the role of phosphatases in the early events after infection with CMV.

human cytomegaloviruses contain protein phosphatase 1 and protein phosphatase IIa, which are derived from host cells.
CMV is a vector of a cellular protein phosphatase.
CMV contains PP1 and PP2, and that the latter is a cellular protein that has been incorporated into the virus.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CMV is capable of transporting active protein phosphatases to cells, which may have a role in the regulation of host cell gene expression.
CMV is a virus that is able to transport active protein phosphatases from one cell to the other.
human cytomegaloviruses contain protein phosphatases that are derived from the host cells and that are transported to the target cells during the viral infection.

CMV is a virus that is able to package a protein phosphatase in the virus particles.
